header: The top headlines: business (The Economic Times, Mint, BusinessLine, WSJ), steel (hunted in many papers through news searches) or general news in English, Hindi or Bengali, from the publishers' own free feeds (src/lib/live/news.ts). The only thing I read from the caller is the tab, and only from a fixed list (biz, steel, en, hi, bn); anything else is English. Feeds that do not answer are left out and named. WHAT A CARD MAY SHOW (the owner's rules, news.ts applyFacts): a story with no picture is not shown, and a story that needs a subscription is not shown. Both are read from the story's own page (pageFacts.ts), for the stories at the top of the tab first, and further down the list only when too few stories are left. HOW IT STAYS QUICK:

* all feeds are asked AT THE SAME TIME, and one that has not answered in 3 seconds does not hold the others up: its last good answer is used (or it is left out and named) and it goes on loading in the background;

* a tab is FRESH for 30 minutes, or 5 while it holds a priority story reported in the last three hours; from 80% of that time, the first asking is answered at once from what is kept while the next is made in the background (memoSwr), up to three hours old before anybody waits; the pages already read are kept a day, so a rebuild reads only the stories that have just appeared;

* BREAKING NEWS BREAKS THE RULE (newsWatch.ts): every three minutes, while somebody is looking, a few quick feeds are tested with the priority rules, and a new priority headline makes the language tabs old at once;

* THE OTHER FOUR TABS ARE WARMED (warmOthers): whoever opens the page, after the tab asked for is answered the other four are made ready in the background, two at a time, so that a click on any tab is answered at once from what the server keeps;

* THE FINISHED LISTS ARE SAVED in the database (persist, table live_snapshot: the list with its picture addresses, public headlines only) whenever a new one is had, and a server that starts empty (a restart, a new instance) takes them back as what it keeps when they are less than three hours old, so the first visitor is answered at once too and a new list is made in the background;
* the host's shared cache may keep the response for a minute only, so that it never adds to that age.

symbols.name: TAB_FRESH_MS
doc: How long a tab is fresh: thirty minutes, five while it holds a priority story of the last three hours. A feed is kept two minutes (so that a rebuild, which comes after at least 24 minutes, or after 4 when a tab is hot, always asks the papers again).

symbols.name: TAB_SHORT_MS
doc: A tab that came out short (the time ran out before enough pictures were found; what was found is kept, so the next build gets further) is kept only two minutes.

symbols.name: FEED_DEADLINE_MS
doc: A feed that has not answered in this time is not waited for.

symbols.name: LOOK_AT
doc: How many stories' pages are read at a time, and at most how many times more are looked at when too few stories are left.

symbols.name: keep
doc: Keeps a background job alive after the response has gone (on the host); outside a request (a test) the job just runs.

symbols.name: readOne
symbols.sig: async function readOne(s: ReturnType<typeof READ_OF>[number]): Promise<string | null>
doc: One feed, kept by its address (so that a feed shared by tabs is asked once); one that has not answered in FEED_DEADLINE_MS gives what was kept of it (or nothing) and finishes by itself.

symbols.name: lookForBreaking
doc: The watch: when it is time, reads the quick feeds and, if a priority headline is new, makes the three language tabs old (they are rebuilt in the background at the next asking).

symbols.name: tabOptions
doc: EVERYTHING A TAB NEEDS TO BE SERVED, in one place: serving a tab (GET) and warming one in the background (warmOthers) use these same options, so that they share one kept answer, one saved copy and one build in progress. `persist` with `seed`: the finished list (with its picture addresses) is saved in the database whenever a new one is had, and a server that starts empty takes it back as what it keeps, so the first visitor is answered at once.

symbols.name: warmOthers
doc: WARMING: whoever opens the news page, the other four tabs are made ready in the background (after the tab asked for has been answered), two at a time, so that a click on any tab is answered at once from what the server keeps; a tab already fresh costs nothing (and one past 80% of its time is refreshed ahead), one the database has a copy of is taken from there first. Asked at most every 20 seconds.
